subject: Platform adaptor interop: tech alignment & engineering asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@integralai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T15:05:00Z
Subject: Platform adaptor interop: tech alignment & engineering asks

Samir — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so engineering can scope the adaptor work.

Key pain we heard
- High tail latency on your current embedding+rerank pipeline when traffic spikes (esp. long documents).
- Need deterministic structured outputs for downstream routing (product classification + confidence fields).
- Existing infra uses serverless workers; they want to avoid large model VMs per request.

Goals you stated
- Get a streaming/funcall-enabled SDK experience that can output structured JSON incrementally.
- Drop per-request token cost by ~30% using caching/batching and a lighter rerank model for first-pass.
- Prototype in Q4 with integration tests and a short POC run.

Integration surface we discussed
- SDK changes: small adaptor layer in your Python microservices to call Redwood's streaming endpoint, with an optional local prefix cache and token-budget hints.
- Function calling: use funcalls for extraction tasks (entities, confidence, category) so you can avoid parsing heuristics.
- Streaming: stream tokens + structured funcall output to update product taxonomy in real time.
- Embeddings/rerank: two-stage flow — embeddings for recall (low-cost quantized model), fast rerank for top-K with Redwood-hosted variant.

Engineering asks (for scoping)
1) Sample payload: example request/response shapes and current average payload sizes. (see attached example-payloads.json)
2) Latency SLOs: P95 target per request and acceptable batch delay.
3) Traffic profile: baseline qps and expected burst multiplier.
4) Security: are there external IP restrictions or a VPC requirement for the POC?

Attachments
- integration-scope.pdf (high-level proposal)
- example-payloads.json (sample request/response)

Proposed next steps
- You confirm the payload and SLO info (items 1–3) by EOD Thu 10/23.
- We’ll produce an engineering runbook + minimal SDK adaptor story by Mon 10/26.
- Schedule 30m sync with your Dev lead to walk the runbook (I’ll propose slots).

Thanks again — excited to move to a quick POC.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Samir Patel <samir@integralai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: IntegralAI Dev Team <dev-team@integralai.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T16:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Platform adaptor interop: tech alignment & engineering asks

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few points and answering the quick questions below.

Quick confirmations
- Latency: P95 target is <= 350ms for the rerank step; we can tolerate up to ~600ms with backpressure.
- Traffic: steady-state 45 qps, bursts up to 250 qps for short periods during index refresh.
- Security: POC can use a dedicated subnet; we’ll provide CIDR allowlist. For production we will need VPC peering.

Items you asked for
1) Sample payload: attached. Note we typically send documents up to 8k tokens but average is ~1.2k.
2) SLOs: see Latency above; token budget per request target ~1.5k tokens.
3) Bursts: traffic multiplier 5–6x.

One ask from our side
- If you can provide an example of streaming structured output (funcall example) from Redwood SDK that shows incremental confidence updates, that would help our QA plan.

I’ll get the network contact and CIDR by tomorrow. Happy to hop on the sync as well.

—
Samir Patel
Head of Platform, IntegralAI
samir@integralai.com
[Attachment: example-payloads.json (JSON)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@integralai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T20:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Platform adaptor interop: tech alignment & engineering asks

Samir — perfect, thanks for the details. A few clarifications and our engineering plan now that we have the numbers: 

Clarifications
- When you say "rerank step" P95 <=350ms, is that end-to-end (embeddings + rerank) or only the second-stage rerank model? We interpreted that as second-stage only.
- For doc sizes: 8k max — do you have a strict hard limit or will truncation be acceptable for the POC?

Engineering plan (POC scope)
- Day 0–2: Runbook + example SDK adaptor (Python) that plugs into your worker pattern. Includes streaming funcall demo producing incremental JSON (we'll include an annotated trace).
- Day 3–7: POC deploy to private test subnet with CIDR allowlist, automatic batching and prefix cache enabled.
- Day 8–14: Load test at 5x baseline to validate batching and burst handling + latency tuning.

Tech notes for your team (what we will deliver)
- SDK adaptor: small shim that exposes two high-level calls — stream_classify_funcall() and embed_and_recall(). Both accept token hints and a cache key.
- Streaming funcalls: we’ll show a stepwise output that includes {"entities":[], "category": "", "confidence": 0.0} updates and a final resolved payload.
- Rerank flow: we recommend an on-host quantized embedder for recall (to reduce tokens) + Redwood-hosted rerank model for quality. We’ll provide recommended top-K settings and latency/cost tradeoffs.

Deliverables we’ll upload to the shared doc
- Runbook (how to wire SDK adaptor into your workers)
- Sample traces and simulated load report
- Acceptance criteria for the POC (latency, correctness on structured outputs)

I’ll upload the draft runbook to the Google doc and DM a few proposed times for the sync.

—
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
[Link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-integration-plan]

Samir — Karthik from Redwood engineering here. Following up on a couple of actionable engineering items before we kick the POC: 

1) CIDR allowlist: please send the test-subnet CIDR and the expected source ports for outbound connections. We will provision the test nodes accordingly.
2) Example payload: I reviewed the attached payloads. For the first POC run we’ll set the embed recall top-K to 200 and rerank top-K to 10. That gives a good balance for quality vs latency.
3) Streaming funcall example: attached below is an annotated snippet we will include in the runbook:
